newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Buba M3 decision good for EMU efforts.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Buba M3 decision good for EMU efforts.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday welecomed the Bundesbank's decision to tighten its target for M3 money growth and to extend the period it covered to two years as a good basis for Europe's single currency.
"With this decision the German Bundesbank underlines its commitment to making a contribution towards creating a stable European currency in a united Europe," Waigel said in a statement.

Waigel said the new M3 target of 3.5-6.5 percent, slightly tighter than the current 4-7 percent, would allow sufficient liquidity in the market for economic growth while simultaneously setting the stage for European monetary union.

"In the view of the federal government, the Bundesbank creates good pre-conditions that will help its proven money supply concept find appropriate resonance in the future monetary policy of the European Central Bank," he said.
He added that the Bundesbank's decision to tighten the M3 target also showed that it was committed to preventing any excess liquidity in the markets ahead of monetary union.
